population: Expanded-lattice / multi-copy occlusion (calibrated on FoldKit experimental S-layer lattices, bacterial and archaeal: open hexagonal arrays through dense lattices; use for any expanded lattice, not only S-layers)
rounding: Bands are rounded outward. When a 5-point grid would reduce a positive LOI/contact minimum to zero, the lower limit uses a 1-point grid instead; upper limits use a 5-point grid. BSA/kDa uses 5 units at both edges.
notes: Occlusion bands are empirical: FoldKit LOImolA measures burial of one focal chain by ALL neighbours in a multi-copy 2-D lattice, so monomeric 3-D crystal-packing statistics (Carugo & Argos 1997: 15-49% of surface in crystal contacts, mean ~27%) are not transferable.
Mode name 'bbox' signals general expanded-lattice use; the calibration cohort is experimental S-layers until a non-S-layer expanded cohort is available.

The LOI and contact-residue lower bounds are nonzero empirical reference baselines, not claims that an assembled lattice can have no contacts. Their observed minima (2.3% and 2.7%) are rounded outward to 2%, while upper limits retain the coarser 5-point reporting grid.

S-layers are porous meshworks (typically 30-70% porosity, pores ~2-8 nm; Sleytr et al. reviews), and much of each subunit faces solvent on the environment and cell-wall sides, so absolute occlusion is expected to be low with a meaningful compact-versus-open spread.

Cohort spans compact C. difficile SlpA-type lattices (narrow ~8-11 A pores; Lanzoni-Mangutchi et al. 2022) and permeable arrays such as Sap and archaeal hexagonal S-layers (~30-100 A openings), which set the upper and lower ends of the band respectively.
BSAmolA/kDa remains correlated with LOI (BSA/kDa = LOI x isolated_SASA/kDa) and varies with subunit size and architecture even at similar LOI, so it is banded but not independent.
